title: Plassere bare, også, selv og til og med — focus-particle scope
goal: Place focus particles so the included, added, restricted, or singled-out constituent is clear.

objectives.statement: Place focus particles so the included, added, restricted, or singled-out constituent is clear.

spans.value: Sofie is arranging dinner at a rented cabin. Jonas wants to know who is coming and what each person will bring.
Bare Amir kommer klokka seks. De andre kommer senere.

blocks.translation: Only Amir is coming at six. The others are coming later.

spans.value: Nei, også Liv kommer klokka seks.

blocks.translation: No, Liv is coming at six too.

spans.value: Amir tar bare brød. Liv tar også ost.

blocks.translation: Amir is bringing only bread. Liv is bringing cheese as well.

spans.value: Men Liv liker jo ikke sterk ost.

blocks.translation: But Liv doesn’t like strong cheese, as you know.

spans.value: I kveld tar hun til og med blåmuggost.

blocks.translation: Tonight she is even bringing blue cheese.

spans.value: Ja, selv Liv vil prøve den.

blocks.translation: Yes, even Liv wants to try it.

spans.value: Four short expressions organize much of this conversation:
The position of each small word tells us what Sofie is restricting, adding, or presenting as surprising.

sections.title: What does the particle point to?

spans.value: ). A focus particle highlights one part of a sentence. Its
is the word or group of words that it points to.

no.value: Bare Lea møter oss på kafeen.

en.value: Only Lea is meeting us at the café.

no.value: Lea møter bare oss på kafeen.

en.value: Lea is meeting only us at the café.

no.value: Lea møter oss bare på kafeen.

en.value: Lea meets us only at the café.

spans.value: The basic event remains similar, but the restriction moves:

items.value: restricts the person who meets us;

statement.value: Put the focus particle immediately before the word or phrase it is meant to highlight whenever that placement is possible.

spans.value: Norwegian main-clause word order still applies. If a focused phrase begins the sentence, the finite verb remains in second position:
forms the first part of the sentence, followed by

en.value: 'Not: Only Lea is coming today. (in this situation)'

spans.value: The particle does not cancel ordinary main-clause word order.

en.value: Only Amir is coming at six.

spans.value: . Liv, Sofie, and the others are excluded from the group described as coming at six—until Sofie corrects or expands the information.
Here the restricted information is the time. In a suitable context, this could contrast six o’clock with other possible times.

en.value: Only Nora is working on Friday.

no.value: Bare vi kjenner den nye læreren.

en.value: Only we know the new teacher.

no.value: Vi kjenner bare den nye læreren.

en.value: We know only the new teacher.

no.value: Oskar kjøper kaffe bare på lørdager.

en.value: Oskar buys coffee only on Saturdays.

spans.value: In the first sentence, other people are excluded. In the second, other days are excluded.
The first sentence restricts who knows the teacher. The second restricts which teacher or person we know.
The first sentence restricts what Oskar buys. The second restricts when he buys it.

sections.title: A common mistake: assuming bare belongs to the whole sentence

spans.value: in one familiar position without checking the intended contrast.
This does not mean that dessert is Liv’s only purchase. It means that no one except Liv is buying dessert.

. It adds one person, thing, place, or other constituent to an existing set.
In the dialogue, Jonas already knows that Amir is coming at six. Sofie adds Liv:

en.value: Liv is coming at six too.

spans.value: stands first. Because this is a main clause, the verb follows it:

en.value: Liv is bringing cheese as well.

spans.value: is added to what Liv is bringing. Bread or another item is already understood, and cheese joins the list.

en.value: Daniel is visiting Bergen as well.
The neighbors are getting an invitation too.
The neighbors are also getting a gift.

spans.value: Daniel is added to the people visiting Bergen.
Bergen is added to the places Daniel visits, assuming the context has already mentioned another place.
The first sentence adds the neighbors to a group of recipients. The second adds a gift to what the neighbors receive.
can sometimes depend on context or spoken emphasis:
This might be understood as adding coffee to Mina’s purchases, or as adding Mina’s coffee-buying to other known facts. When a contrast must be unmistakable in writing, place
directly before the added noun phrase:
The first explicitly adds Mina. The second most naturally adds coffee in a context about Mina’s purchases.

sections.title: Marking a surprising inclusion with selv and til og med

spans.value: . They show that someone or something is included despite being unexpected.
In the cabin dialogue, Liv normally dislikes strong cheese. This makes her choice surprising:

en.value: Even Liv wants to try the blue cheese.

no.value: Til og med Liv vil prøve blåmuggosten.

en.value: Even Liv wants to try the blue cheese.

spans.value: . Other people may be willing to try it, but Liv is the least expected member of that group.
Til og med Liv vil prøve blåmuggosten.
is especially clear and flexible before different kinds of phrases:

no.value: Liv tar til og med blåmuggost.

en.value: Liv is even bringing blue cheese.

no.value: Vi spiser ute til og med i november.

en.value: We eat outside even in November.

no.value: De inviterte til og med den nye sjefen.

en.value: They even invited the new boss.

spans.value: In each sentence, the phrase after
is compact and common before a focused person or group:

en.value: Even the children liked the soup.
Even the teacher forgot the date.
Even the neighbors heard the music.

sections.title: A common mistake: confusing focus selv with “himself/herself”

spans.value: . It emphasizes that Liv did the work personally.
Position changes the message completely. Before
, the word marks Liv as a surprising participant. After
, it emphasizes that Liv acted without someone else doing it for her.

no.value: Liv spiste til og med desserten.

spans.value: The intended surprise is the dessert, not the person who performed the action.
Jonas writes a summary for the group:
Bare Liv kjøper dessert, og Amir kjøper også brød.

blocks.translation: Only Liv is buying dessert, and Amir is buying bread as well.

spans.value: Den første delen er feil. Amir kjøper også dessert. Liv kjøper bare dessert.

blocks.translation: The first part is wrong. Amir is buying dessert too. Liv is buying only dessert.

spans.value: foran personen, men jeg mente tingen.

blocks.translation: Oh yes. I put “only” before the person, but I meant the thing.

spans.value: Nettopp. Og skriv at til og med naboene kommer etter middagen.

blocks.translation: Exactly. And write that even the neighbors are coming after dinner.

spans.value: Kommer også naboene? Da blir vi mange!

blocks.translation: Are the neighbors coming too? Then there will be a lot of us!

prompt.value: Choose the complete interpretation that correctly identifies the scope of bare, også, til og med, and selv in the supplied cabin-dinner sentences.

options.text: Bare and også describe the whole sentence without a focused constituent. Til og med adds blue cheese, while selv means only Liv. The English translations are only Amir, Liv too, only bread, cheese as well, even blue cheese, and even Liv.
options.why: The option gives translations but does not identify the actual particle scope and misstates the functions of til og med and selv.

options.text: “Bare Amir kommer klokka seks.” restricts klokka seks. “Også Liv kommer klokka seks.” adds klokka seks. “Amir tar bare brød.” means Amir is bringing bread as well. “Liv tar også ost.” restricts ost. “I kveld tar hun til og med blåmuggost.” presents hun as surprising. “Ja, selv Liv vil prøve den.” means Liv did the action herself.
options.why: The option assigns particles to the wrong constituents and confuses focus selv with personal-action selv.

options.text: “Bare Amir kommer klokka seks.” means “Only Amir is coming at six”: bare restricts Amir. “Også Liv kommer klokka seks.” means “Liv is coming at six too”: også adds Liv. “Amir tar bare brød.” means “Amir is bringing only bread”: bare restricts bread. “Liv tar også ost.” means “Liv is bringing cheese as well”: også adds cheese. “I kveld tar hun til og med blåmuggost.” means “Tonight she is even bringing blue cheese”: til og med marks blue cheese as surprising. “Ja, selv Liv vil prøve den.” means “Yes, even Liv wants to try it”: selv marks Liv as surprising.
options.why: The interpretation identifies the focused person or thing for every particle and gives the intended English meaning.

prompt.value: In cabin preparations, build the Norwegian sentence meaning “Nora works only on Friday.” Put bare directly before the restricted time and keep normal main-clause word order.

explanation.value: Place the focus particle immediately before what it restricts or adds: «bare på fredag», «også ost», and «til og med blåmuggost».

prompt.value: Compare the paired messages and choose the interpretation that explains the scope contrast and the alternatives excluded in each sentence.

options.text: “Bare Liv kjøper dessert.” means “Liv is buying only dessert”: bare restricts dessert. “Liv kjøper bare dessert.” means “Only Liv is buying dessert”: bare restricts Liv.
options.why: The option reverses the scope of bare in both sentences.

options.text: “Bare Liv kjøper dessert.” means “Only Liv is buying dessert”: bare restricts the person and excludes other people from buying dessert. “Liv kjøper bare dessert.” means “Liv is buying only dessert”: bare restricts what Liv buys and excludes other purchases.
options.why: Moving bare changes whether the excluded alternatives are other people or other purchases by Liv.

options.text: Both sentences mean “Liv is buying only dessert” because bare always restricts the object, regardless of its position.
options.why: Particle placement determines scope; bare does not always restrict the object.

stem.value: Which interpretation correctly explains both sentences?

prompt.value: Build the Norwegian update meaning “Liv is bringing cheese as well.” Bread is already known, so place også directly before the added object.
The intended meaning is “Liv is bringing cheese as well.” The current message is “Også Liv tar ost.” Find the one particle token whose placement communicates the wrong addition.

payload.feedback: Også focuses on Liv here, so it adds a participant. Move også before ost to add cheese instead: “Liv tar også ost.”

prompt.value: During the cabin evening, build the Norwegian sentence meaning “Tonight she is even bringing blue cheese.” Place the supplied particle til og med directly before the surprising food.
The intended meaning is “Even Liv made the food.” In the message “Liv lagde maten selv.” find the one token whose placement gives the personal-action meaning instead of the even meaning.

payload.feedback: Selv follows maten, so it means that Liv did the work herself. For the intended even meaning, place selv before Liv and capitalize it: “Selv Liv lagde maten.”

prompt.value: Write four original short Norwegian updates about a workplace picnic. Make these meanings explicit: (1) only one employee attends, with bare before the restricted participant; (2) a food, time, or place is added to an established picnic plan, with også before the added constituent; (3) an unexpected person participates, with selv before that person; and (4) a different food, time, or place is surprising, with til og med before that constituent. Make each focus scope clear through placement.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: Uses bare before the participant being restricted in one workplace-picnic update.
Uses også before the constituent being added in one workplace-picnic update.
Uses selv before an unexpected person in one workplace-picnic update.
Uses til og med before a different surprising food, time, or place in one workplace-picnic update.
Places each particle so the restricted, added, or surprising constituent is clear.

prompt.value: Create two pairs of original Norwegian sentences about one workplace picnic. In pair one, keep the core event broadly constant but shift bare from restricting which employee brings salad to restricting what that employee brings. In pair two, keep the core meeting event broadly constant but shift også from adding a participant to adding the meeting location. After the pairs, explain each scope contrast briefly in Norwegian.

criteria.instruction: Provides a sentence pair where bare shifts restriction from a participant to an item while the core picnic event remains constant.
Provides a sentence pair where også shifts addition from a participant to a location while the core meeting event remains constant.
Explains in Norwegian which constituent is restricted or added in each sentence.
Uses particle placement intentionally rather than repeating one memorized position.

prompt.value: Write exactly four original short Norwegian sentences about planning a workplace lunch. Use one sentence to restrict a person or thing with bare, one to add a different constituent with også, one to mark a surprising person with selv, and one to mark another surprising constituent with til og med. Underline the constituent each particle highlights.
